psalmBeforeIfPriestTitle: If there is a priest, he says
psalmBeforeIfPriest: Blessed is our God, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages
psalmBeforeIfLaymanTitle: But if not, say with contrition
psalmBeforeIfLayman: Through the prayers of our holy fathers, O Lord Jesus, Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen.
psalmBeforeGloryThee: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
psalmBeforeTroparion:
Troparia, tone 6: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us, for devoid of all defense, we sinners offer unto thee as Master this prayer: Have mercy on us.

Glory: The honorable celebration of thy prophet, O Lord, hath shown the church to be heaven, as with men exult the angels. By his prayers, O Christ God, direct our lives in peace, that we may sing to thee: Alleluia.

Both now: Great is the multitude of my transgressions, O Theotokos: unto thy purity I have recourse, seeking salvation; visit my soul in mine infirmity, and pray thy Son our God to grant me the remission of mine evil deeds, O thou who alone art blessed.
psalmBeforePrayerTitle: Then this prayer to the holy and life-creating Trinity
psalmBeforePrayer: All holy Trinity, God and Creator of the whole world: Come and direct my heart to begin with understanding, and to end with good works, this divinely inspired book which the Holy Spirit uttered through the lips of David, and which I now desire to recite, unworthy though I am. Knowing well my own ignorance, I fall down before thee and pray, beseeching thy help, O Lord! Direct my mind and make my heart steadfast, that I may not grow weary because of the words which my lips read; but that I be gladdened with the understanding of what is read, and myself prepared for the doing of the good works which I learn. And so I say, “Enlightened by good deeds, may I become a citizen of the land, which is at thy right hand, with all of thine elect.” And now, O Master, bless me, that, having sighed from my heart, I may sing with my tongue, saying:
psalmBeforeSuggestion: Then wait a little, until all the senses are quieted. Then begin without haste, without sloth, with compunction and a broken heart, to say "Blessed is the man..." quietly and intelligently, attentively, and without rushing, so that the mind understands the words.
